artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan replacing both git-lint enumeration sites with a shared tracked-plus-untracked union library carrying loud stderr skip diagnostics, with acceptance fixtures in both lint suites.

memory_candidates.content: A lint or gate that enumerates its scan corpus via `git ls-files` reports a FALSE CLEAN for any file that exists on disk but is not yet git-tracked: the index returns zero rows, an on-disk existence guard (`-e`) still passes, the scan loop never iterates, and the summary prints a clean verdict with no diagnostic. This defeats exactly the self-hygiene check a newly created file most needs (a new blocking hook linting its own source before committing it). Remedy pattern, already precedented in this repo by script-inventory.sh: enumerate the UNION of `git ls-files <scope>` and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard <scope>`, `sort -u`. `--exclude-standard` keeps gitignored build output and the disposable deployed tree excluded, so the union does not widen scope. Pair it with three stderr-only diagnostics so silence is never a possible third outcome: a per-file loud skip naming each on-disk file the union still excludes and why, an untracked-inclusion count disclosure, and a zero-enumeration warning when a scope exists on disk but enumerates nothing. Keep diagnostics off stdout and out of any `info()`/`--quiet` path, so exit codes and stdout formats stay byte-identical for gate consumers. When auditing for this defect, distinguish genuine instances from scripts where untracked-ness is the signal being measured rather than a blind spot.
